# Background Verification for Real Estate and Construction Companies in India: RERA Compliance and Site Safety \[2026\]


September 22, 2026


[Shashank Yadav](https://salarybox.in/blog/author/shashank87cc9f270b/)


[No comments yet](https://salarybox.in/blog/background-verification-for-real-estate-and-construction-companies-in-india-rera-compliance-and-site-safety-2026/#respond)


Background verification for real estate and construction companies in India is a regulatory, safety, and liability necessity because the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2016 (RERA) holds developers accountable for project delivery and professional standards, the Building and Other Construction Workers Act 1996 mandates worker safety protections, and site environments with heavy machinery, heights, and hazardous materials amplify the consequences of deploying unverified workers with false identities or fabricated experience claims. Digital verification of PAN, Voter ID, DL, and UAN through platforms like Compose1 Verify takes minutes per worker and provides the audit-ready documentation that RERA authorities, labour inspectors, and insurance companies require.


India’s real estate sector is one of the largest employers in the country, contributing approximately 7 to 8 percent of GDP and employing an estimated 70 to 80 million workers directly and indirectly. The construction workforce includes civil engineers, site supervisors, crane operators, plumbers, electricians, masons, carpenters, painters, welders, scaffolders, earthmoving equipment operators, labourers, security guards, and administrative staff.


The sector also employs thousands of real estate brokers, property managers, facility managers, and back-office staff who handle customer data, financial transactions, and legal documentation.


The common characteristic across all of these roles is access: access to construction sites with inherent safety hazards, access to customer personal and financial information, access to project funds, and access to residential and commercial properties. Each of these access points creates risk that background verification mitigates.


Yet the construction industry has among the lowest verification rates of any sector in India. The contractor brings 50 labourers to the site on Monday morning. The site manager checks if they can do the work. Nobody checks who they actually are. When one of those labourers causes an accident, steals materials, or is involved in a site fatality, the developer discovers that the identity on the muster roll is fictitious.


## Regulatory Framework for Real Estate and Construction


### RERA 2016


The Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act requires developers to register projects with the state RERA authority, maintain transparency in project dealings, and adhere to professional and ethical standards. While RERA does not explicitly mandate employee background verification, it establishes a regulatory framework that holds developers accountable for the professionals they engage.


RERA-registered projects are subject to audits by the RERA authority. During these audits, the authority may examine the developer’s compliance with various regulations, including labour laws. Having verified employee records demonstrates regulatory seriousness and due diligence.


Real estate agents and brokers must be registered under RERA. The registration process includes identity verification requirements. Developers working with unregistered or unverified brokers risk RERA compliance issues.


### Building and Other Construction Workers (BOCW) Act 1996


The BOCW Act is the primary legislation governing construction worker safety and welfare. It requires registration of construction workers, safety protections, and welfare measures. The Act applies to construction establishments employing 10 or more workers.


Under the BOCW Act, the employer is responsible for ensuring the safety and health of construction workers. This responsibility implicitly includes ensuring that workers operating dangerous machinery and working at heights are qualified and properly identified.


### Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act 1970


Construction relies heavily on contract labour. Most site workers are deployed through labour contractors. Under the CLRA Act, the principal employer (developer or construction company) bears significant liability for contract workers, including their safety and welfare.


### Factories Act 1948


Pre-cast concrete plants, ready-mix concrete (RMC) plants, steel fabrication units, and other manufacturing facilities operated as part of construction projects fall under the Factories Act. Workers in these facilities need identity verification under the same framework that applies to manufacturing.


### Motor Vehicles Act 1988


Construction sites use heavy vehicles: dumpers, transit mixers, cranes, JCB/backhoe loaders, bulldozers, road rollers, trucks, and various material transport vehicles. Every operator must hold a valid DL for the appropriate vehicle class. Deploying an unlicensed operator on a construction vehicle violates the Motor Vehicles Act and creates uninsured liability.


## The Construction Site Verification Challenge


### Migrant and Transient Workforce


Construction has the most mobile workforce in India. Workers move from site to site, city to city, and state to state following projects. A worker who was in Hyderabad last month is in Pune this month and will be in Ahmedabad next month. They often carry minimal documentation and rely on contractors to manage their paperwork.


This transience makes verification both more difficult and more important. The worker’s previous site has no connection to the current site. There is no employment continuity. Each site is a fresh start where the worker presents whatever identity they choose. Without independent verification, each site accepts whatever the contractor provides.


### Multi-Layered Contracting


Construction projects typically involve multiple layers of contracting. The developer hires a main contractor. The main contractor hires sub-contractors for specific trades (electrical, plumbing, masonry, etc.). Sub-contractors hire workers, often through labour contractors. By the time a worker reaches the site, they have passed through 3 to 4 organizational layers, none of which may have verified their identity.


The developer, who bears the ultimate RERA and safety liability, is the furthest removed from the worker’s actual identity.


### High-Risk Environment


Construction is among the most dangerous occupations in India. Falls from height, crane accidents, scaffolding collapses, electrical injuries, trench cave-ins, and equipment malfunctions cause thousands of injuries and deaths annually. When an unverified worker is involved in a fatality, the investigation faces an identity void. The developer cannot cooperate fully with police because the worker’s real identity is unknown.


### High Theft Risk


Construction sites store valuable materials: steel, cement, copper wire, fixtures, fittings, and equipment. Material theft from construction sites is a significant cost issue for developers. Workers operating under fake identities can steal materials and disappear without a trace.


## What to Verify Across Real Estate Roles


### Construction Site Workers (All Trades)


**Every worker on every site needs identity verification.**


**PAN Verification:** Confirms identity against the Income Tax Department database. Essential for TDS compliance (TDS applies to contractor payments and, in some cases, individual worker wages above threshold).


**Voter ID Verification:** Cross-confirms identity through the Election Commission database. The cross-record analysis catches workers using borrowed or stolen identity documents, which is common in the transient construction workforce.


**How to do it:** Enter PAN and Voter ID numbers on[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Results in 2 to 10 minutes. Cost: Rs 100 to Rs 400 per worker.


### Heavy Equipment and Vehicle Operators


**DL Verification is non-negotiable for every equipment operator.**


Crane operators, JCB operators, bulldozer operators, dumper drivers, transit mixer drivers, tower crane operators, and any worker who operates motorized equipment on or around the construction site must have their DL verified against VAHAN/SARATHI.


**What to verify:** Licence validity (not expired), suspension status (not suspended), vehicle class authorization (heavy vehicle operators need HMV or specific class authorization), and the name matches other identity documents.


**How to do it:** Add DL verification on[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Results in 2 to 5 minutes. Cost: Rs 50 to Rs 200 additional.


**Re-verification:** Quarterly for all operators. Construction projects run for months or years. A DL that was valid at the project start can expire or get suspended mid-project.


### Site Engineers and Supervisors


**UAN employment history verification confirms claimed experience.**


Site engineers, project managers, quality engineers, safety officers, and supervisors are hired based on experience. A “10-year experienced” site engineer commands a significantly higher salary than a 3-year engineer. If the experience is fabricated, the project gets an underqualified person in a role that affects structural integrity, safety compliance, and project timeline.


**How to do it:** Add UAN verification in the Compose1 Verify session. Results in 5 to 30 minutes. Cost: Rs 200 to Rs 500 additional.


### Real Estate Brokers and Sales Staff


Real estate brokers and sales executives handle customer personal information, property documents, and financial transactions. An unverified broker can commit financial fraud, misrepresent properties, or misuse customer data.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID for identity confirmation. RERA registration verification (separate from Compose1 Verify, checked on the state RERA website).


### Property Management and Facility Staff


Property managers, maintenance staff, security guards, and housekeeping staff deployed at residential and commercial properties have access to occupied spaces, resident data, and building systems.


**Required checks:** PAN + Voter ID for all staff. DL for drivers and transport staff. These individuals work in residential complexes where families, including children and elderly residents, are present. Identity verification is a basic safety measure.


## Construction-Specific Scenarios


### Scenario 1: The Crane Operator with an Expired DL


A developer in Noida hires a crane operator through a sub-contractor for a 40-storey residential tower project. The operator’s DL expired 5 months ago, but nobody checked. During a lift operation, the operator misjudges the load capacity and the crane boom fails, dropping a steel beam onto a partially completed floor. Two workers are injured. The insurance company investigates and discovers the expired DL.


Result: Insurance claim denied (Rs 15 lakh in damage and medical costs fall on the developer). Labour inspector issues notice under BOCW Act. RERA authority receives a complaint about safety violations. The developer faces potential criminal liability.


A DL verification costing Rs 100 would have caught the expired licence before the operator touched the crane controls.


### Scenario 2: Material Theft by Workers with Fake Identities


A construction company in Bangalore reports that approximately Rs 12 lakh worth of copper wiring, steel fixtures, and bathroom fittings have gone missing over 3 months from a commercial project. CCTV shows workers loading materials into vehicles after work hours. When the company tries to identify the workers from their records, they discover that 4 of the workers provided PAN numbers that belong to people in other states. The workers used fake names, collected wages, stole materials, and are untraceable.


PAN + Voter ID verification for all site workers would have flagged the identity mismatches before these workers received site access badges.


### Scenario 3: The Site Engineer Who Caused Structural Issues


A real estate developer hires a “Senior Structural Engineer” at Rs 80,000 per month based on a resume claiming 12 years at three major construction firms. The engineer supervises foundation work for a residential complex. During a quality audit 6 months later, structural defects are discovered in the foundation that require Rs 45 lakh in remediation work. Investigation reveals the “engineer” had 2 years of actual experience as a junior site supervisor (not an engineer) at one construction firm.


UAN verification would have shown EPFO records with only 2 years of contributions from one employer, not 12 years from three.


## Implementing Verification in Construction Projects


### For Developers (Principal Employer)


**Before project launch:** Establish a verification policy that applies to all workers on all project sites. Include the policy in all contractor and sub-contractor agreements.


**During project execution:** Require all contractors to submit worker document numbers (PAN + Voter ID + DL for operators) before workers enter the site. Run verification through[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . Issue site access only after verification.


**For sales and marketing staff:** PAN + Voter ID for all broker and sales staff. Confirm RERA registration for brokers.


### For Main Contractors


**Worker deployment:** Verify all directly employed workers before deployment. For sub-contractor workers, require sub-contractors to provide document numbers and either verify them yourself or require verified reports before allowing site access.


**Equipment operators:** DL verification is mandatory before any operator touches any equipment. No exceptions. Maintain a register of verified operators with DL expiry dates. Schedule re-verification 30 days before expiry.


### For Sub-Contractors


**Compliance with principal employer requirements:** Submit all worker document numbers to the principal employer or main contractor as required. Cooperate with independent verification requirements. Maintain your own verification records.


### For Labour Contractors


**Worker onboarding:** Verify every worker’s identity (PAN + Voter ID) before deploying them to any site. Cost per worker through Compose1 Verify: Rs 100 to Rs 400. This cost is part of the deployment overhead and can be factored into contract pricing.


## Cost Analysis for Construction Projects


### Small Residential Project (50 Workers Over 18 Months)


PAN + Voter ID for all workers: 50 x Rs 300 = Rs 15,000. DL verification for 10 equipment operators: 10 x Rs 200 = Rs 2,000. Quarterly DL re-verification for operators (6 quarters): 10 x 6 x Rs 150 = Rs 9,000. UAN for 5 engineers and supervisors: 5 x Rs 500 = Rs 2,500. **Total project verification cost: Rs 28,500.**


For a project with a budget of Rs 10 crore, the verification cost is 0.03 percent.


### Large Commercial Project (500 Workers Over 3 Years)


PAN + Voter ID for all workers (including turnover replacements, approximately 700 total): 700 x Rs 300 = Rs 210,000. DL verification for 80 equipment operators: 80 x Rs 200 = Rs 16,000. Quarterly DL re-verification (12 quarters): 80 x 12 x Rs 150 = Rs 144,000. UAN for 50 engineers and supervisors: 50 x Rs 500 = Rs 25,000. **Total project verification cost: Rs 395,000 (Rs 3.95 lakh).**


For a project with a budget of Rs 200 crore, the verification cost is 0.002 percent.


### Property Management Company (200 Staff Across 20 Properties)


PAN + Voter ID for all staff: 200 x Rs 300 = Rs 60,000. DL for 30 drivers and transport staff: 30 x Rs 200 = Rs 6,000. Annual re-verification: 200 x Rs 150 = Rs 30,000. **Total annual cost: Rs 96,000.**


## Building a Construction Verification Policy


### Policy Elements


**Scope:** All workers, engineers, staff, and contractors on all project sites.


**Minimum checks:** PAN + Voter ID for everyone. DL for equipment operators and drivers. UAN for engineers, supervisors, and experienced hires.


**Timing:** Before site access is granted. No worker enters the site without completed identity verification.


**Responsibility:** Site manager or project HR is responsible for collecting document numbers and running verification. For large projects, a dedicated verification coordinator manages the process.


**Documentation:** PDF verification reports stored in the project file. Worker verification register maintained at the site office. Reports available for RERA inspections, labour inspections, and insurance audits.


**Re-verification:** Annual PAN for long-term workers. Quarterly DL for operators. Immediate re-verification after any safety incident.


**Non-compliance consequences:** Workers without verification are not permitted on site. Contractors who deploy unverified workers receive a warning; repeated violations result in contract termination.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is background verification required for construction workers in India?


The BOCW Act holds employers responsible for worker safety and welfare, which courts interpret to include ensuring workers are qualified for their assigned tasks. The Motor Vehicles Act requires valid DL for equipment operators. RERA establishes accountability standards for developers. While no single law says “verify every construction worker,” the combined regulatory framework makes identity verification a practical and legal necessity.


### How do I verify migrant construction workers who may not have standard documents?


Most workers, including migrant workers, have PAN and Voter ID. PAN is increasingly common due to financial inclusion initiatives and banking requirements. Voter ID is available to any Indian citizen over 18. Verify whatever documents are available through[Compose1 Verify](https://compose1.com/verify/) . If a worker has neither PAN nor Voter ID, assess whether the risk of deploying an entirely unverifiable individual on your construction site is acceptable.


### Should developers verify workers hired by sub-contractors?


Yes. Under the CLRA Act and BOCW Act, the principal employer (developer) bears liability for all workers on the site, regardless of who hired them. Require all sub-contractors to submit worker document numbers before deployment. Run independent verification through Compose1 Verify. Do not rely on the sub-contractor’s claims.


### How much does it cost to verify construction site workers?


PAN + Voter ID costs Rs 100 to Rs 400 per worker through Compose1 Verify. Adding DL for operators costs Rs 200 to Rs 600 total. For a project with 100 workers, total verification cost is Rs 10,000 to Rs 40,000. For a project budgeted at Rs 50 crore, this is 0.008 percent of the project cost. Essentially a rounding error.


### How often should construction equipment operators’ DLs be re-verified?


Quarterly at minimum. Construction projects run for 1 to 5 years. A DL can expire or get suspended at any point during the project. A quarterly check through Compose1 Verify costs Rs 50 to Rs 200 per operator and takes 2 minutes. This protects against insurance denial and Motor Vehicles Act violations for the entire quarter.


### What verification do real estate brokers need?


PAN + Voter ID for identity confirmation through Compose1 Verify. RERA registration verification through the state RERA website. Brokers handle property transactions worth crores and access customer financial and personal data. An unverified broker operating under a fake identity creates both fraud risk and RERA compliance issues.


### Can small builders and contractors afford verification?


At Rs 100 to Rs 400 per worker, verification is affordable for any size of construction operation. A small builder with 20 workers spends Rs 2,000 to Rs 8,000 on verification. Compose1 Verify requires no subscription, no contract, and no minimum volume. You pay only when you verify. The alternative (deploying unverified workers and hoping nothing goes wrong) costs significantly more when something does go wrong.


### What records should construction projects maintain for worker verification?


For each worker: PAN verification report (PDF from Compose1 Verify), Voter ID verification report (PDF), DL verification report (for operators), verification date, contractor and sub-contractor details, site allocation, and consent form. Maintain a site verification register. Keep records for the duration of the project plus two years. These records satisfy BOCW Act, RERA, and insurance documentation requirements.
